You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From e0d4675789499b5955aa05ef9abc2926b30ba4ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2014 11:29:09 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] kill: fix bug in --all semantic

Introduces by 2ab6683f59cd3371b1c3ac8b5c248d5104ed4d41.

Signed-off-by: Karel Zak <kzak@redhat.com>
---
 misc-utils/kill.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/misc-utils/kill.c b/misc-utils/kill.c
index 37f4c6e34..d461b36a6 100644
--- a/misc-utils/kill.c
+++ b/misc-utils/kill.c
@@ -486,7 +486,7 @@ int main(int argc, char **argv)
 
 			if (!ps)
 				continue;
-			if (ctl.check_all)
+			if (!ctl.check_all)
 				proc_processes_filter_by_uid(ps, getuid());
 
 			proc_processes_filter_by_name(ps, ctl.arg);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect condition check for the `--all` option in the `kill` command implementation. The original code checked if `ctl.check_all` was true, which would lead to filtering processes by UID only when `--all` was not specified. The fix changes the condition to check if `ctl.check_all` is false, ensuring that when `--all` is specified, the filtering by UID is skipped, allowing the command to operate on all processes as intended.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect condition check for the `--all` option in the `kill` command implementation. The original code checked if `ctl.check_all` was true, which would lead to filtering processes by UID only when `--all` was not specified. The fix changes the condition to check if `ctl.check_all` is false, ensuring that when `--all` is specified, the filtering by UID is skipped, allowing the command to operate on all processes as intended.
